alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued September 22 at 2:48PM HST until September 26 at 6:00PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
alerts.description:
A potential tropical cyclone is expected to bring heavy rain to the
eastern end of the state over the coming days. The track of this
potential storm is uncertain, but heavry rain is likely.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Maui, Lanai, Molokai, The Big Island and Kahoolawe.

* WHEN...From Wednesday afternoon through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Flood prone roads and other low lying areas may be closed
due to elevated runoff and overflowing streams. Urban areas may
receive more significant flooding and property damage due to rapid
runoff.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy rain on the north side of a developing tropical system (the
future Nolo) should develop Wednesday afternoon. Windward and
southeast Big Island and windward Maui are the most likely to
experience heavy rain. However, other islands in Maui County are
at risk as well, and therefore are included in the watch. Very
high rainfall rates, which can cause flash flooding, are possible
within the entire watch area.
alerts.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 PM HST Tue Sep 22 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, about 200 miles offshore of southern Mexico, and on Tropical
Storm Odalys, located well west-southwest of the southern tip of
Baja California.

Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands (Former TD 15-E):
Showers and thunderstorms associated with the remnants of Tropical
Depression Fifteen-E, located a few hundred miles south-southeast
the Big Island of Hawaii, have become better organized.
Environmental conditions remain conducive for development, and a
tropical depression could form tonight or Wednesday while the system
moves slowly west-northwestward. Heavy rains associated with this
system are forecast to spread over the southeastern Hawaiian Islands
starting on Wednesday and continuing through Saturday, possibly
resulting in life-threatening flash flooding and mudslides for
portions of the Big Island and Maui. Interests in the Hawaiian
Islands should continue to monitor the progress of this system.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...90 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

$$
Forecaster Kelly
NNNN
aiBriefing: Obecnie obowiązuje ostrzeżenie przed powodzią (Flood Watch) dla wielu obszarów Hawajów, w tym Maui i Big Island — ważne od 22 września do 26 września. To ostrzeżenie oraz związany z nim system pogodowy (przyszły "Nolo", obecnie depresja tropikalna Fifteen-E) powinny zakończyć się na długo przed Waszym wylotem, bo do rozpoczęcia podróży zostało 9 dni, a zdarzenie dotyczy najbliższych kilku dni. Oznacza to, że to konkretne ryzyko powodziowe raczej nie będzie miało wpływu na Waszą podróż zaczynającą się 2 października na Oahu, potem Big Island i Maui. Mimo to warto pamiętać, że w tym rejonie regularnie powstają nowe systemy tropikalne (CPHC podaje 90% szans na nowy cyklon w ciągu 7 dni), więc sytuacja może się zmienić — polecam sprawdzić prognozę ponownie bliżej daty wylotu. Na razie poziom zagrożenia jest podwyższony, ale nie ma podstaw do zmiany planów podróży.
